summary: Makes parse() tolerate padded YAML values and documents and tests the compound format. The compound output still uses spaces, so it is not yet ParseDuration-compatible.
narrative: The owner opened with a change of plan: compound output has to work with a Go scraper that uses time.ParseDuration, so it needs glued parts like `25h30m` with hours as the biggest unit. They deferred that and asked first for parse() to tolerate leading and trailing whitespace, because YAML configs often produce it. parse() now trims its input (obs 7), a test was added and committed as b14e8e4 (obs 8-9). Four minutes later a second conversation asked to wrap up the compound format option with README docs and more tests. That added a README section and boundary tests in commit d57cff2 (obs 10-11), and removed a vacuous round-trip assertion that only passed because parse() returned NaN for spaced input (obs 12). The suite passes at 182 tests. The ParseDuration-compatible output change itself has not been made, and there is no evidence of a review, merge or release.

milestones.text: parse() trims input so padded values like ' 2d' and '1.5h ' no longer return NaN

Removed a vacuous round-trip assertion; the full suite passes at 182 tests
